text:
Maria Chen: Proposal: introduce a lightweight 'sentinel' layer that lives between rollout-controller and the router to coordinate canary checks + a rollback handshake. Short version: sentinel evaluates probe signals, holds a short lease, and issues an explicit rollback/commit call to router.
Samir Patel: sketch? how does this differ from the current probe+observer? seems similar to 'observer' services we've had.
Maria Chen: Good q. Difference is sentinel is stateful for the duration of the canary, exposes a tiny contract (lock/verify/commit/rollback) and keeps evaluation logic close to telemetry windows. Goal is to avoid racing decisions across distributed observers.
Devon Lee: I like stateful lease. Concerns: cost of keeping sentinel per-canary. Could be a sidecar per rollout-controller instance instead of per-canary.
Anya Ortiz: SLO noise caveat: if sentinel uses raw per-request latency it will flip too often. Need smoothing + min-sample window. Also rate-limit rollback to avoid thrash.
Maria Chen: Agreed. Proposal includes two mechanisms: 1) signal smoothing (EWMA over 30s) and 2) cooldown circuit: min 5m between automatic rollback actions for a given route.
Cody Nguyen: Product question: will customers see more 'automatic rollbacks' alerts? We need UX controls: opt-in auto-rollback, and severity channels for canary vs production rollback.
Maria Chen: Yes. Default off for self-serve; on for enterprise with SLA guardrails. We'll add audit logs and a human approval toggle.
Devon Lee: Interface sketch (gRPC):
```
service Sentinel {
  rpc Lock( LockRequest ) returns ( LockReply );    // reserve canary lease
  rpc Verify( VerifyRequest ) returns ( VerifyReply ); // pass/fail + metrics snapshot
  rpc Commit( CommitRequest ) returns ( CommitReply ); // finalize rollout
  rpc Rollback( RollbackRequest ) returns ( RollbackReply ); // trigger fallback
}
```
Samir Patel: What does LockReply contain? lease_id, expires_at, observed_baseline_hash?
Maria Chen: yes: { lease_id, expires_at, baseline_hash, allowed_rollout_pct } — baseline_hash helps ensure we compare the right metric set.
Anya Ortiz: Telemetry cost: we should avoid high-cardinality probes per request. Use aggregated counters + sampled traces. Sentinel should accept both streaming samples and periodic summaries.
Maria Chen: Example minimal config that the rollout controller would send when starting a canary:
```
{
  "route": "/api/generate",
  "target_pct": 10,
  "observe_metrics": ["p99_latency", "error_rate"],
  "thresholds": {
    "p99_latency": {"delta_pct": 35, "min_samples": 200},
    "error_rate": {"absolute": 0.01, "min_samples": 100}
  },
  "cooldown_secs": 300
}
```
Cody Nguyen: Nice. Also add a field for 'user_visible_reason' so when rollback happens we can decorate the alert.
Devon Lee: Implementation options: sentinel as a separate control-plane service (multi-tenant) vs ephemeral per-cp sidecar. Tradeoffs: multi-tenant saves memory but centralizes failure domain; sidecar reduces blast radius but increases resource count.
Maria Chen: Long-term we probably refactor into a controller-side subsystem with pluggable adapters: local-sidecar adapter for on-prem, central-managed adapter for hosted. Want same contract either way.
CanaryBot: deploy: canary-sentinel v0.1 rolled to staging
Samir Patel: next steps: prototype sidecar adapter, run 100 canaries in staging with sampled traces + EWMA, measure false positive rollback rate.
Anya Ortiz: also add a 'suppressible' flag so oncall can mute auto-rollback for an incident window.
Maria Chen: Agreed. I'll draft a short RFC with: contract + sample config + telemetry sizing and two-prototype plan (sidecar then central). Will sync w/ infra and product.
Cody Nguyen: Thanks — cc @support for alerting UX
Maria Chen: thanks all :thumbsup:
